newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Stock prices fell after a report of a strong rise in February housing starts prompted fears the Federal Reserve would raise U.S. interest rates.
* Goldman, Sachs reported a first quarter pretax profit of $905 million, up 60 percent.
* News Corp is said to have offered $400 million for PointCast, an Internet broadcaster, but PointCast wants more money.
* More Americans are dying in crashes involving a car and a light truck instead of two cars.
* February housing starts rose 12.2 percent to the highest level in nearly three years.
* A Federal appeals court ruled criminal price-fixing charges could be brought against foreign companies even if crimes took place outside the United States.
* German steelmaker Krupp-Hoesch said it would seek to buy rival Thyssen for $8.1 billion.
* Vice President Al Gore faces a tough decision on whether to preside over signing of China's billion-dollar Boeing-777 purchase next week, in light of campaign finance rumblings.
* NASD investigates nine brokerage firms and trading in 19 small copmanies for possible organized crime links.
* IBM chief executive Louis Gerstner Jr's salary was cut by $5,000 from last year's pay of nearly $5 million.
* Japanese stock prices rose after the government took steps to help banks get rid of bad loans.
* Jacor Communications plans to buy EFM Media Management, which distributes conservative Rush Limbaugh's radio talk show, for undisclosed terms.
* Novell names Sun Microsystems' chief technology officer Eric Schmidt as chairman and chief executive.
* Texaco, and Shell Oil agree to combine refining and marketing operations in the midwest and western United States.
* Market Place: Investors are starting to question the hefty share prices of the once high-flying technology stocks.
* Today's hostile takeovers are driven by a corporate strategy rather than by speculators looking for short-term profit.
